title: [YouPass Collect] - Water Usage and Income from Agricultural Products in Australia: 2004
prompt: The charts below show the use of water for agricultural products in Australia in 2004 and the value of these products to the Australian economy in the same year. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The two pie charts compare the proportion of water consumed by seven agricultural sectors in Australia in 2004 with the percentage of revenue these sectors contributed to the national economy in the same year.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was a significant disparity between water consumption and economic contribution across most agricultural products. Most notably, while livestock was the largest consumer of water, it generated one of the smallest shares of income, whereas the opposite was true for fruit.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the sectors that used more water than the revenue they generated, livestock accounted for the highest proportion of water usage at 36%, yet it contributed a mere 6% to the agricultural income. Similarly, rice consumed 5% of water but yielded only 1% of the total revenue, making it the least profitable product relative to its water consumption. Sugar and cotton followed a comparable pattern, with their water usage standing at 10% and 15% respectively, both slightly higher than their corresponding income figures of 7% and 13%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, fruit demonstrated the most efficient water-to-income ratio, as it required only 11% of water while generating a substantial 44% of agricultural revenue, making it the most economically valuable product. Dairy also showed a positive balance, with water consumption at 19% and income contribution at 24%, representing a difference of 5 percentage points. Finally, vegetables exhibited a relatively balanced profile, using 4% of water and producing 5% of the total income.
